title: Recover gamma from losses
goal: Appendix M shows how to read $N_{\text{eff}}$ from measured losses. The loss gap between a run at weight precision $P_w$ and a full-precision run at the same $(N, D)$ is $A\left[N_{\text{eff}}^{-\alpha} - N^{-\alpha}\right]$, because the $B$, $D$, and $E$ terms cancel. Write `n_eff_fraction(loss, loss_inf, n)`, which solves that gap for $f = N_{\text{eff}} / N$ (Equation 30). The constants `A` and `ALPHA` are defined in the starter. Then write `fit_gamma(ps, fracs)`, which fits $f(P) = 1 - e^{-P/\gamma}$ and returns `gamma`. The tests build synthetic losses from a known $\gamma$, so a correct fit recovers it.
hints: Solve the gap for $N_{\text{eff}}$: $N_{\text{eff}}^{-\alpha} = (L_P - L_\infty)/A + N^{-\alpha}$. Raise both sides to $-1/\alpha$, then divide by $N$.
At full precision the loss gap is 0, and the formula must return exactly 1. Use that as a check.
Take logs of $f = 1 - e^{-P/\gamma}$. Then $\ln(1 - f) = -P/\gamma$, which is a line through the origin with slope $-1/\gamma$.
The least-squares slope of a line through the origin is $\sum P y / \sum P^2$ with $y = \ln(1 - f)$. Then $\gamma = -1 / \text{slope}$.
